question: Attribute the ~23 MB/cycle by diffing two snapshots taken at the SAME collapsed state, one cycle apart.
verdict: Each multichart cycle permanently retains ONE panel realm's entire script set: +20.87 MB of script source and +63 Script objects per cycle, which is 89% of the 23.53 MB/cycle floor growth. Two of the three peer realms are collected; one is not.
config: deployed, PO workload, 4 DISTINCT symbols @1m, forced-GC floors, 3 cycles
cycleCountIsThreeOnPurpose: Snapshots serialize to ~2.3x usedJSHeapSize and JSON.parse dies above V8 max string length. The two snapshots here are 304 MB (cycle 2) and 353 MB (cycle 3) and both parse. 6 cycles (~560 MB) dies. Nothing is truncated.

instrument.what: Takes a heap snapshot after the collapse of each of the last two cycles, so both readings sit at the same collapsed state (single chart, one live realm) with the same forced-GC treatment. The 1-realm-to-4-realm warm-up cancels instead of being counted as recurring.
instrument.whyNeeded: W76-P2B and W77 both read a baseline-vs-final diff, which spans the warm-up. This is the measurement W77 named as the next step.
instrument.alsoAdded: assessScriptRealmGrowth() diffs two censuses directly, so the verdict needs no assumption about how many realms a cycle creates — which is exactly where W77 went wrong.

floors.note: The pair is measured one cycle apart at identical state, so 23.53 MB is a true per-cycle figure, not a mean that includes warm-up.

externalStringDataSplit.reading: All 20.87 MB of the ExternalStringData growth is script source. The non-script external strings are FLAT at 0.50 MB. Whatever else is suspected, it is not growing.

perUrlCopyCounts.reading: The histogram shifts wholesale: 52 URLs held 3x become 53 URLs held 4x. Every shared module gains exactly one copy per cycle.

correctionToW77.whatIClaimed: W77 said per-realm script source is a BOUNDED ~62 MB and not the per-cycle term, on the falsifier 'x4 after three cycles, not x10'.
correctionToW77.whyThatWasWrong: The x10 expectation assumed that leaking would mean retaining all three peer realms every cycle (1 + 3*3). The actual rate is ONE realm per cycle, which produces 1 + 3 = 4 copies at three cycles — indistinguishable from bounded retention in a single snapshot, and only separable by diffing two snapshots.
correctionToW77.howItWasCaught: The cycle-2 vs cycle-3 histograms: 52 URLs at x3 become 53 at x4. A single end-of-run snapshot cannot see that shift, which is why the model-free two-census diff now exists.
correctionToW77.netEffect: W76-P2B's original attribution — script source and compiled code — was RIGHT. My W77 retraction of it was wrong, for a different reason than the original was uncertain. The rate is now measured rather than inferred: 20.87 of 23.53 MB per cycle.
correctionToW77.whatStandsFromW77: The x4-per-URL duplication, the 61.7 MB of redundancy at any moment, the retainer chain naming, and the refutation of cache-shaped retention (non-script external strings flat at 0.50 MB) all hold.

mechanismForManagerA.statement: Every cycle expands four panels as four iframes, each its own realm compiling the full chart bundle (~21 MB of source). On collapse all three peer iframes are destroyed. Two of those realms are collected; ONE is retained permanently, with its complete script set plus the compiled-code family (InstructionStream +3.48 MB, BytecodeArray, FeedbackVector, ScopeInfo, constant pool).
mechanismForManagerA.rate: 20.87 MB/cycle of source + ~5.5 MB/cycle of compiled artefacts and other objects = 23.53 MB/cycle measured at the floor.
mechanismForManagerA.retainerChainFromW77: ExternalStringData <- source string <- system / Script / <url> <- SharedFunctionInfo / <fn> <- closure <- Window [JSGlobalObject] own property <fn> <- system / NativeContext, with the realm context pinned from (Eternal handles) via FunctionTemplateInfo -> WeakMap -> DOMTokenList.
mechanismForManagerA.whatIsStillUnnamed: WHICH of the three peer realms survives, and what distinguishes it. Candidates worth one run each: the last-focused panel, the panel that received the order placement, or the panel holding the indicator worker. Narrowing that names the specific teardown path that fails to release.
mechanismForManagerA.whyDatasetCountMattered: With four identical panels the four iframes share one resource identity and the configuration plateaus; with four distinct symbols each realm is distinct and one is retained per cycle. That is why the leak scales with distinct dataset count, as the Director's ~67 MB vs ~367 MB observation predicted.
